Windows one-file release of VBA Add-in Editor. The ZIP contains `VBAAddinEditor.exe` and its SHA-256 checksum file.

## Design the ribbon without touching XML

The ribbon now has a view of its own: click the ribbon icon in the side rail, press **Ctrl+2**, or choose **Ribbon → Design Ribbon**. The side rail now lists four views in this order: **Code**, **Ribbon**, **UserForms** and **Package XML** (**Ctrl+1** to **Ctrl+4**).

- **Left:** the ribbon as a tree (tab › group › menu › button), with a filter. The line at the bottom says how many macros are linked, or how many callbacks still need a macro. Click it to show only those.
- **Right, top to bottom:** a drawing of the tab; a form for the selected control (Label, Macro, Icon, Size, Screentip, Supertip, Id and any other callbacks); and the code of the macro it runs. Press **F12** or double-click to open that macro in the Code view.

Adding a button takes no dialog:

- **+** or **Ins** adds a button where the selection is, and the cursor goes to **Label**. The button's id follows its label until you give it one yourself. The **+** menu also adds a menu, group or separator.
- Type or pick a macro under **Macro**. A plain `Sub X()` gets a small `XCallback(control As IRibbonControl)` wrapper. A name that doesn't exist shows **Create Sub**.
- In the tree: **Alt+Up/Down** moves a control, **Del** deletes (it asks first if a group or menu still holds controls), **F2** renames. Drag a control before, after or into another; drops that Office wouldn't accept are refused. Select several controls to delete them or group them into a menu.

Each change is one **Undo** step and an ordinary edit of the ribbon XML. The rest of the XML stays exactly as it was, and **Edit XML** shows the control in the Package XML view. A ribbon part open there has a **Design view** button that goes back to it.

Built-in (`imageMso`) icons can't be drawn offline, so the drawing shows a placeholder for them and your own picture for custom icons.

## Procedures beside the code

Under the module list, **PROCEDURES** lists the open module's Subs, Functions (`fn`) and properties (`get`/`let`/`set`) and follows the cursor. Macros a ribbon control runs carry a ribbon mark. **+** adds a new Sub; right-click adds a ribbon button for the macro or shows the one it has.

## Other changes

- The ribbon outline panel beside the XML and the M/A/R legend under the module list are gone; the designer and the outline replace them.
- Ribbon commands (Add Button, Add Menu, icons, Import Button, F12 from the code) show their result in the ribbon view you used last, designer or XML.
- Fixed: after switching to the light theme, the **Filter** hint in the side lists kept a dark background.

## Checked in Office

A new `.xlam` and a new `.pptm` were built in the designer. Each got two buttons (one with a built-in icon, one with a custom picture), a menu holding a button, a separator and a second group, and two controls were moved by dragging. Both were then saved and opened in Excel and PowerPoint. Each opened with no repair prompt, the ribbon's `onLoad` ran, the tab showed both icons, and pressing each button, including the one inside the menu, ran its macro.

## Notes

- This is a development build, built and tested on GitHub's Windows runner. It has not been through the full live Excel/PowerPoint qualification matrix. Keep the automatic backup on.
- In those checks the drags were sent to the tree as events, not made with a hand on the mouse.
- Known bug: a module whose code starts with a blank line fails save verification ("Body mismatch"). The original file is left untouched; remove the leading blank line and save again.
- Password-protected VBA projects remain read-only.
